title: migrations.zig has no tenant-only scope primitive — 13 PER_TENANT shadow tables from ISS-0641 will keep recurring on cold-start
notes: Discovered incidentally while resolving ISS-0641/GH-637 (14 dual-schema shadow tables). GBL-141 cleans the 14 shadows, but for 13 of the 14 (PER_TENANT tables whose canonical home is tenant_default), the fix is cleanup-only: src/db/migrations.zig::migrationScope() has no primitive that suppresses just the public-pass copy of a table while keeping the tenant_default-pass copy. The only two scopes are .public_only (GBL- filename prefix or a `-- scope: public` header) and the default .all_schemas. Confirmed by live reproduction: after a full cold-start `zig build migrate` + `zig build test-integration` replay (which provisions fresh tenant schemas), tenant_artifact_activations (the 1 GLOBAL_REGISTRY table in ISS-0641, same problem in the opposite direction) reappeared in tenant_default even with GBL-141 applied and recorded in the ledger -- the ledger only prevents GBL-141 itself from re-running, not migration 058_repo_artifacts_tenant_activation.sql (a .all_schemas-scope file, correctly so for its other table repository_artifacts which is HYBRID) from creating a fresh shadow in any newly-provisioned tenant schema. Manually restored db_test to steady state for this run's completion; the underlying gap remains.
candidate_resolution: 1. Add a third MigrationScope value (e.g. .tenant_only, selected by a new `-- scope: tenant_only` header) that runs a migration file in every per-tenant schema pass but skips the public pass entirely -- the mirror of the existing .public_only primitive. 2. Apply it to the source migrations creating GBL-141's 13 PER_TENANT tables so public-pass creation stops permanently. 3. For migration files that mix classifications in one file (like 058_repo_artifacts_tenant_activation.sql: HYBRID repository_artifacts + GLOBAL_REGISTRY tenant_artifact_activations), either split into two new migration files (each single-scope) or design a per-statement/per-table annotation mechanism -- evaluate cost/benefit, this is the larger of the two options. 4. Extend tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py (or a new pre-merge lint per ISS-0641/GH-637 suggestion #3, also not yet built) to flag when a corrective GBL migration exists to clean a shadow but the creating source migration still has no scope primitive that would prevent recurrence, making this class of "cleanup only, not closed" defect visible without a live cold-start reproduction. Severity MINOR: does not block current pipeline operation -- the corrective-migration pattern (GBL-134 through GBL-141 in this lineage) is well-established and low-cost to re-apply on each recurrence; this is a structural/DX improvement to end the recurring detect-clean-recur cycle, not a live defect.
resolution: Implemented candidate resolutions (1) and (2) for the tractable subset. src/db/migrations.zig gains MigrationScope.tenant_only, selected by a new `-- scope: tenant_only` header (mirror of `-- scope: public`), plus the symmetric skip in runForSchema's apply loop (skip tenant_only migrations in the public pass, mirroring the existing public_only skip in tenant passes). Applied the header to the 3 of 13 PER_TENANT source migrations that are genuinely single-purpose (create exactly one table, no other statements): 026_ext05_subprocess_links.sql, 093_exp103_instance_waits.sql, 095_iss0176_lua_script_execution_audit.sql. The other 10 PER_TENANT tables' source migrations (019, 012, 008, 004, 007, 010) each create multiple tables of MIXED classification in one file (e.g. 008_identity.sql creates both GLOBAL_REGISTRY `users`/`roles`/`api_tokens` and PER_TENANT `sessions`/`user_groups`/`group_roles`/`role_permissions`) -- a whole-file tenant_only header would incorrectly suppress the GLOBAL_REGISTRY tables' public-pass creation, so these were left untouched; GBL-141's cleanup-only fix remains their active mitigation. Candidate resolution (3) (splitting mixed files or a per-statement scope mechanism) and (4) (a pre-merge structural lint) were NOT implemented -- out of scope for this fix, left as documented future work in src/design/fix-ISS-0644.md.
verification: Live cold-start reproduction: docker-compose rm -f -s -v db_test (db_test only) + up -d (genuinely empty volume) + zig build migrate (BPM_DB_URL pointed at test port, 121 migrations applied) + zig build test-integration-ext02 (provisions tenant_default fresh, 10/10 pass) + tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py -- 0 duplicated table names (previously showed the recurring shadows including subprocess_links/instance_waits/lua_script_execution_audit). zig build test-integration-adp02 (4/5, same pre-existing unrelated TC-ADP-02-01 failure) and test-integration-exp (13/13) confirmed no regression. zig build test 89/89 steps, 1011/1075 pass (64 skipped, same as baseline +2 new passing unit tests for the new scope value). zig build migrate idempotent (second run: 0 applied). lint_sql_param_types.py 0 findings. db_test restored to clean, fully-migrated steady state.
prevention: The two new unit tests in tests/unit/db_test.zig (TC-DB-01-08) lock in migrationScope()'s tenant_only classification and confirm GBL- prefix still wins over any tenant_only header, matching the existing precedence-order tests for public_only.

src/design/fix-ISS-0644.md documents exactly which of the 13 PER_TENANT source migrations are safe for a whole-file scope header (single-purpose) vs which are not (mixed classification) -- a future author extending this fix to more tables has the classification methodology and the specific per-file reasoning already written down, rather than needing to re-derive it.
